proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity shows that for such a prime \(p\), \(5\) is a square modulo \(p\); choosing a suitable square root \(x\) and setting \(n=x-1\) gives \(3\le n<p\) and \(p\mid n^2+2n-4\). Writing the continued fraction as \(N_2/N_3\) with \(N_2=n^2+2n-4=pq\), recurrence divisibility identities show that \(q\) divides \(N_3\) while \(p\) does not, so reduction cancels exactly the cofactor \(q\) and leaves numerator magnitude \(p\).
